title: Etale locality and base change of relative perfectness
statement: Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived direct image is computed by K-injective resolutions, and derived tensor pullback by K-flat resolutions. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a flat locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$. An object $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ is $Y$-perfect if it is pseudo-coherent (on etale affine charts represented by bounded-above complexes of finite free modules) and locally has finite Tor amplitude over $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y$. The latter means locally there are integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring $K$ over this ring sheaf, in the derived sense, with every module in degree zero has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. This property is etale local on $X$ and $Y$ and implies quasi-coherent cohomology. For any morphism of algebraic spaces $g:Y^{\prime}\to Y$, putting $X^{\prime}=X\times_Y Y^{\prime}$ and $g^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to X$, a $Y$-perfect $K$ has $Y^{\prime}$-perfect derived pullback $L(g^{\prime})^*K$.

proof.text: For a commutative chart diagram $U\xrightarrow h V$, $U\to X$, $V\to Y$ with etale vertical maps, the ring $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y|_U$ identifies with $h^{-1}\mathcal O_V$: etale pullback of the structure sheaf is restriction [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pseudo-coherence is local by the stated bounded-above finite-free-model definition: restriction retains a model, and models on a covering constitute local models on $X$. The Tor condition can be tested on geometric stalks by [lem-sfb-space-ring-sheaf-tor-amplitude-stalk-test]; restriction to charts keeps the same stalk rings by [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness]. Therefore an interval valid on a chart is exactly an interval for the restricted object over the indicated inverse-image ring. Local intervals may differ from chart to chart. Coverings of charts compose to coverings, so these two local conditions can be checked on any jointly surjective etale presentation. This proves the stated etale locality on source and target.

source.place: Tag 0DKQ (lemma-affine-locally-rel-perfect), locality argument, with pseudo-coherence in the local-model form of the item.

proof.text: On a chart with finite-free model $P^\bullet$ for $K$, each $P^i$ is quasi-coherent by its finite free presentation [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], $Z^i=\ker d^i$, $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$ and $Z^i/B^i$ are quasi-coherent, using the kernel, image and cokernel clauses. The last quotient is $H^i(K)$ on the chart. Quasi-coherence is local by its definition, hence $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. No coherent-kernel theorem over a Noetherian ring is being used.

source.place: Tag 08JL (lemma-pseudo-coherent), calculation of cohomology from finite free local models.

proof.text: The fibre product is an algebraic space, and etale covering presentations remain covers after pullback [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Flatness of $f'$ follows from [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. For local finite presentation, take etale scheme presentations $U\to X$, $V\to Y$ with a map $U\to V$ and $U\to X$ surjective. Such diagrams exist by [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion], and $U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation. Cover $Y'\times_Y V$ by etale schemes $V'_j$; then $U\times_VV'_j\to V'_j$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], clause (3). These are jointly surjective etale source charts of $f'$, so the same presentation criterion proves that $f'$ is locally of finite presentation. Thus relative perfectness over $Y'$ is defined with the hypotheses in force.

Put $K'=L(g')^*K$. Choose the finite-free models for $K$ on etale charts and pull their covering back to $X'$. On any scheme chart $W$ refining a pulled-back chart $U$, a model $P^\bullet$ is bounded above and termwise flat, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Restriction preserves K-flat resolutions by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-restriction-kflat]. Consequently tensor pullback of this model computes $K'|_W$; the local tensor formula is precisely the pullback specified by [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. In degree $i$ it sends $\mathcal O_U^{r_i}$ to $\mathcal O_W^{r_i}$ and sends a matrix differential to the matrix obtained by applying the structure-ring map. It therefore remains bounded above and finite free. Thus $K'$ is pseudo-coherent; this proves the claim directly rather than citing a new relative-perfectness clause.

source.place: Tag 0DKT (lemma-base-change-relatively-perfect); finite-free pullback calculation of pseudo-coherence, as in perfect.tex second proof of lemma-base-change-relatively-perfect.

proof.text: Finally take any chart on which $K$ has relative Tor interval $[a,b]$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-tor-independent-relative-amplitude] to its pulled-back square: its flat-case clause applies because $f$ is flat, while $g$ remains arbitrary. It gives the same interval for $K'$ over $(f')^{-1}\mathcal O_{Y'}$ on the pulled-back chart. These charts cover $X'$, so $K'$ locally has finite relative Tor amplitude. Together with the pseudo-coherence just proved and the flat locally finitely presented morphism $f'$, this is exactly $Y'$-perfectness. The zero complex and empty charts satisfy the same argument, with interval $[0,0]$ if needed.
